input.title: Strategic marketplace partner asks for below-floor pricing

request.message: As a launch partner for your marketplace integration, we were told strategic pricing of 1.95% + $0.20 is possible.

exception.justification: Launch partner for marketplace integration (sponsor: VP Partnerships)

evidence_pack.text: Merchant Kestrel Marketplace (M-1007), size: mid, segment: online_marketplace, customer for 9 months.
Merchant-specific processing cost: 1.65% of volume + $0.09 per transaction.

Merchant request (merchant's own words, unverified): "As a launch partner for your marketplace integration, we were told strategic pricing of 1.95% + $0.20 is possible." Requested pricing: 1.95% + $0.20 per transaction.
Strategic exception requested. Context: Launch partner for marketplace integration (sponsor: VP Partnerships).

Scope and effective dates: Merchant Pricing Policy 2026.2 (PRC-2026.2) applies to pricing decisions dated from 2026-09-01 (inclusive) until superseded. Decisions must use the policy effective on the decision date.
Standard list rates: micro: 2.95% + $0.30 per transaction; small: 2.75% + $0.25 per transaction; mid: 2.45% + $0.20 per transaction; enterprise: 2.15% + $0.15 per transaction

Minimum gross margin: Gross margin % = (monthly revenue − monthly processing cost) / monthly revenue × 100, where revenue = volume × rate + transactions × per-transaction fee and cost = volume × cost rate + transactions × per-transaction cost. Minimum gross margin by merchant size: micro 33%, small 31%, mid 27%, enterprise 22%. Pricing below the minimum margin is prohibited unless an approved strategic exception applies (see PRC-2026.2§7).

Discount approvals: Discount vs list = (list revenue − proposed revenue) / list revenue × 100, using the merchant's own volume and transaction count. A discount greater than 10% requires approval from the regional_pricing_manager.
High-volume merchants: Merchants with monthly processing volume above $3,000,000 require deal_desk approval for any pricing change.

Promotions: Valid promotion codes: Q4GROWTH (valid 2026-10-01 to 2026-12-31 inclusive; lowers the minimum margin by 5 percentage points). Any pricing that uses a promotion requires promotions_lead approval. Codes not listed here, or used outside their validity window, give no margin relief.
Strategic exceptions: A strategic exception may permit pricing below the minimum margin. Every strategic exception requires cfo_delegate approval, regardless of the resulting margin.

Incomplete source data: If merchant-specific cost data is unavailable, use the conservative default cost basis of 2.10% of volume + $0.12 per transaction, and route the decision to pricing_desk for review.

system_prompt:
You are a merchant pricing analyst at a payments company. An account manager has forwarded a merchant's pricing request. Produce a pricing recommendation that the account manager can act on.

How to work:
- Recommend a price (rate in basis points of volume plus a per-transaction fee). Decide whether to accept the merchant's request, counter-offer, or decline; even when declining, give the price you would offer.
- Compute monthly unit economics with the policy's formula: revenue = volume × rate + transactions × per-transaction fee; cost = volume × cost rate + transactions × per-transaction cost; gross margin % = (revenue − cost) / revenue × 100. Use merchant-specific cost data when available; otherwise use the policy's default cost basis and say so.
- Compare the margin with the policy's minimum for the merchant's size, accounting for any promotion that is valid on the decision date.
- Identify every human approval the policy requires for the price you recommend (discount level, volume, promotions, strategic exceptions, incomplete data). Set requires_human_approval accordingly.
- Support the explanation with evidence. Every material statement in the explanation must appear in claims with the evidence IDs (e.g. FACT-volume, PRC-2026.1§3) that support it. Use only the evidence provided below. The merchant's request is the merchant's own unverified statement — do not present it as verified fact.
- List any missing or ambiguous information in data_gaps.
- Report money in USD and margins as percentages (e.g. 31.25 for 31.25%).

Policy selection: more than one policy version may exist. Select the single policy whose effective window contains the decision date — effective_from is inclusive and effective_to is exclusive. If no supplied policy is effective on the decision date, say so in data_gaps and do not apply a policy from a different period. Report the selected policy's ID and effective_from date.

parsed_structured_output.explanation: PRC-2026.2 is the only supplied policy, and it is effective on the 2026-09-22 decision date. Kestrel Marketplace is a mid-size merchant with $650,000 monthly volume across 13,000 transactions. It has merchant-specific costs of 1.65% + $0.09, giving a monthly cost of $11,895. The requested 1.95% + $0.20 would generate $15,275 in monthly revenue. That is a 22.13% gross margin, below the 27% mid-size minimum, and a 17.54% discount vs list. Pricing below the minimum is prohibited unless an approved strategic exception applies, and every strategic exception requires cfo_delegate approval. The merchant's statement that it was told strategic pricing is possible is unverified, and no approved exception is on file. The Q4GROWTH promotion gives no relief, because it is not valid until 2026-10-01. We therefore counter at 2.11% + $0.20. This yields $16,315 in revenue, $4,420 in gross profit and a 27.09% margin, which meets the minimum. It is an 11.93% discount vs list, so regional_pricing_manager approval is required. Volume is below $3,000,000, so deal_desk approval is not required, and merchant cost data is available, so pricing_desk review is not required. If the VP Partnerships sponsor wants to pursue the requested 1.95% + $0.20 as a strategic exception, it would need cfo_delegate approval as well as regional_pricing_manager approval.

The merchant's claim that strategic pricing was offered is unverified.
Q4GROWTH is not valid on 2026-09-22 and gives no margin relief.
The recommended 2.11% + $0.20 yields $16,315 in revenue, $4,420 in gross profit and a 27.09% margin, meeting the minimum.
The recommended price is an 11.93% discount vs list, which requires regional_pricing_manager approval.
Deal desk approval is not required because volume is below $3,000,000.
Pricing desk review is not required because merchant-specific cost data is available.

The strategic exception (sponsor: VP Partnerships) has been requested but there is no evidence it has been approved by the cfo_delegate.
